transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Athena Head of AI), Maya Chen (Eng Manager), Samir Khan (Security Lead)

Summary (auto-gen): AE opened with quick context, SE demoed the Hosted API with chat examples, live streaming and param tweaks, then covered retry logic and error handling. Security questions around data residency and KMS; agreed to run a benchmark POC.

00:00 Speaker 1: hey everyone, thanks for joining, today we'll run through Redwood's hosted api chat and text generation basics, streaming, params and retries. lena?
00:18 Lena Park: yeah thanks, hi ravi, maya, samir. quick agenda: overview, demo in console + curl, streaming example, params tuning, retries/backoff, then q&a and next steps. should be about 30-45 mins.
00:37 Ravi Patel: sounds good. just so you know, we care a lot about latency for our chat features, and cost. We run millions of tokens a month but want 100-200ms p95 for short turn completions, and of course security is big because of pii and payments data.
00:58 Marcus Liu: got it, thanks. we'll show how streaming reduces perceived latency and how batching/caching from Optimize helps with cost.
01:10 Lena Park: i'll share the deck link in chat - redwood-hosted-api-overview.pdf (note: link posted).
01:22 Maya Chen: great, can you show retries? we saw issues with other providers when transient errors cause duplicate charges or repeated ops.
01:35 Marcus Liu: yep, we'll demo typical retry patterns, idempotency token suggestions, and how our client libraries implement exponential backoff.
01:50 Marcus Liu (screen share): ok i'm in the Redwood console - first page is model catalog, then endpoints. i'll open a chat route 'athena-demo-chat' we created earlier.
02:15 Marcus Liu: here's a streaming run - watch the response stream in the browser. notice tokens come in as partial events, we flush to the client every 100-200ms typically, depending on buffer settings. that gives the perception of low latency even if total generation takes a few 100s ms.
02:47 Ravi Patel: when you say flush every 100-200ms, is that configurable? could we do lower for certain routes?
03:00 Marcus Liu: yes it's tunable per route, and we can change flush interval or use chunked mode for larger batches. there's a tradeoff: more frequent flushes increases throughput overhead, small batches can raise cost slightly.
03:20 Maya Chen: what about max tokens and stop sequences? can we set deterministic behavior for templated prompts?
03:33 Marcus Liu: you can set max_tokens, stop, temperature, top_p per request. for templated prompts we recommend low temp (0-0.2) and explicit stop sequences. we also support logprobs and sampling control. here's a curl example...
03:57 Marcus Liu: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"rw-moon-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize..."}], "stream":true, "temperature":0.1, "max_tokens":60}'
04:20 Speaker 2: uh that model string, is rw-moon-1 the smallest? what are the tiers?
04:28 Lena Park: our catalog has model families, and we annotate perf profiles. for most production chat we recommend rw-sky or rw-peak depending on latency/cost needs. we can share the perf spreadsheet.
04:40 Ravi Patel: does Redwood do automatic fallback to cheaper models if primary is overloaded?
04:50 Marcus Liu: yes we have smart routing and fallback policies. you can configure route policy: prefer low-latency, prefer low-cost, or hybrid. if p95 exceeds threshold we can failover to a compatible quantized variant.
05:10 Samir Khan: security question: how long do you keep request logs and are inputs stored by default?
05:23 Lena Park: hosted api by default retains logs for 30 days for debugging, but you can opt into no retention. for enterprise we have configurable retention and data residency options. we also integrate with KMS for customer-managed keys.
05:44 Samir Khan: KMS - do you support AWS KMS and GCP KMS/HSM?
05:50 Lena Park: yes, AWS KMS and Cloud KMS supported; HSM integrations available for Private deployments. we'll attach SOC2 and KMS diagram in follow-up.
06:05 Maya Chen: about retries - can you show how the client handles 429s and 5xx?
06:12 Marcus Liu: sure, here's the client logic: on 429 we do jittered exponential backoff, we include an idempotency key for POST-like operations, and we provide retry-after header handling. i will paste a snippet in chat.
06:32 Marcus Liu: note the typical pattern: initial delay 100ms, multiply by 2, cap at 3s, random jitter +-20%. we also recommend circuit-breaker on the client side for long tail.
06:52 Ravi Patel: do retries ever cause duplicate outputs that matter for us? we need idempotent downstream processing.
07:02 Marcus Liu: for generation endpoints, idempotency tokens help make sure retries don't cause duplicate database writes on your side; the model outputs may differ if generation is retried, so best practice is to make the model call side-effect-free and apply idempotency at the application layer.
07:25 Maya Chen: demo the streaming again but with a higher concurrency so we can see behavior under load.
07:37 Marcus Liu: switching to a scripted load in the console - running 50 concurrent streams with small prompts. you'll see partials come in and the console shows per-token cost estimate.
08:05 Speaker 1: there's a small hiccup, one stream threw a transient 503 - that's where retries kicked in, we rerouted a few to a cheaper quantized node to keep latency.
08:30 Marcus Liu: exactly - the routing layer helped keep the overall SLO. cost delta was minimal.
08:45 Ravi Patel: curious about streaming in mobile clients - is there an SDK for chunked streaming?
08:52 Lena Park: yes our mobile SDK supports incremental events over websockets and a lightweight JS client for chunk handling. we have examples in the repo.
09:05 Maya Chen: can we control how prompt context is cached? we don't want to resend whole history each time.
09:12 Marcus Liu: Redwood supports prefix and KV cache; you can store embeddings or KV pairs on the platform and reference them by key to avoid sending long contexts. note sometimes the transcript shows as K V cash in older docs, sorry for typos.
09:34 Ravi Patel: what's the billing model for streaming? per token as usual?
09:40 Lena Park: yes tokens billed per generation; streaming only changes delivery, not billing. there are also throughput tiers for Reserved/Dedicated customers.
09:50 Maya Chen: Optimize - you mentioned batching and caching suggestions earlier, can you show that?
09:58 Marcus Liu: switching tab to Redwood Optimize - it has workload analyzer, it suggests batch sizes and quantization levels. here's a sample recommendation: for short chat turns, batch size 8 at 2048 context for rw-sky gives best cost/latency tradeoff.
10:23 Marcus Liu: Optimize also surfaces rouge/quality regressions when you change model or quantization, tied to eval prompt sets.
10:40 Ravi Patel: interesting, can Optimize run on our traffic traces or only synthetic?
10:48 Marcus Liu: it can ingest anonymized traffic traces (you can mask PII) or run with sample prompts; we usually run a small offline calibration first.
11:00 Samir Khan: network egress and private data - if we use hosted API, how do we ensure secure peering?
11:08 Lena Park: for enterprise we offer VPC peering and private link options to avoid public internet. plus SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs.
11:20 Maya Chen: timeline question - if we like what we see, how quickly can we start a POC?
11:27 Lena Park: typically we can spin up a POC in 2 weeks for hosted API - we'll need your sample prompts, target SLOs, and a list of stakeholders.
11:40 Ravi Patel: ok we'll get the dataset over. Samir will want the SOC2 and KMS details.
11:50 Lena Park: noted. i'll recap next steps at the end.
12:02 Marcus Liu: one more note on retries: we also surface detailed per-request traces in the console so you can see if retries happened and why.
12:18 Maya Chen: thanks, the trace view will help us debug.
12:30 Marcus Liu: quick live curl demo of retry header handling - sending a request with idempotency key and simulate a 502, watch client backoff.
12:55 Speaker 2: transcription glitch - shows 'rw moon' sometimes, but that's the model namespace.
13:10 Lena Park: ok wrapping up - recap: we'll send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram; Marcus will share benchmark harness and we'll schedule the POC scoping call for 2026-04-05.
13:28 Ravi Patel: yep that works, thanks all.

End transcript.

Notes: transcript includes natural disfluencies and occasional mis-typed product names; references to shared artifacts: redwood-hosted-api-overview.pdf (link), perf-spreadsheet.xlsx (link), SOC2_and_KMS_diagram.pdf (link).
